rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken equivalent for believing or tentatively concluding, especially in “I suppose...”

example.english: I suppose it will rain tomorrow.
example.jyutping: ngo5 lam2 ting1 jat6 wui5 lok6 jyu5

rows.note: Choose this when “suppose” means making an uncertain guess or assumption from incomplete information rather than simply saying what you think.

example.english: I suppose he hasn't arrived yet.
example.jyutping: gu2 keoi5 jing1 goi1 mei6 dou3

rows.note: Use this for the mental-imagining part of “suppose,” when asking someone to picture or imagine something.

example.english: Suppose you imagine what would happen if there were no electricity.
example.traditional: 你想像吓，如果冇電會點？
example.jyutping: nei5 soeng2 zoeng6 haa5 jyu4 gwo2 mou5 din6 wui5 dim2

rows.note: Use this for a deliberate hypothesis or premise, especially in explanations, mathematics, and formal reasoning.

example.english: Suppose all the numbers are positive, then we can continue calculating.
example.traditional: 假設所有數字都係正數，我哋就可以繼續計。
example.jyutping: gaa2 cit3 so2 jau5 sou3 zi6 dou1 hai6 zing3 sou3 ngo5 dei6 zau6 ho2 ji5 gai3 zuk6 gai3
